name: Merge verify focus test
description: Focus test: close+merge-verify under adversarial conditions

nodes.body_template:
## Close — merge ticket branch into master

**Ticket:** ${trigger.title}

The ticket's code lives on branch `ticket-focus` in the repo at `${trigger.card_body}`.

### Step 1: Merge

```bash
cd ${trigger.card_body}
git checkout master
git merge --no-ff ticket-focus
```

If merge conflicts: resolve them.

### Step 2: Run tests

```bash
pytest -q
```

- If ANY test fails: do NOT fix it yourself. Complete with verdict=test_failure and record the failing test names and error output in failing_tests. The workflow will route to the debugger.
- If ALL tests pass: proceed to step 3

### Step 3: Verify no lost work

```bash
git log master..ticket-focus
```

Should output nothing. If commits appear: ESCALATE.

### Complete

**Completion metadata:**
{verdict: "merged"|"test_failure"|"escalated", merged_to: "master", all_tests_pass: true|false, task_count: 2, failing_tests: ""}

## Merge verification — mechanical git + test check

**Ticket:** ${trigger.title}
**Close verdict:** ${nodes.close.output.verdict}

### Your job: PROVE the merge is real, not just claimed.

The repo is at `${trigger.card_body}`. Run these checks.

### Check 1: Branch fully merged

```bash
cd ${trigger.card_body}
git log master..ticket-focus
```

Must output NOTHING. If any commits appear — FAIL.

### Check 2: No dangling commits

```bash
git fsck --unreachable 2>/dev/null | grep commit
```

If ANY commits show up containing 'ticket' or 'fix' — FAIL.

### Check 3: Tests pass on merged master

```bash
git checkout master
pytest -q
```

ALL tests must pass. ANY failure — FAIL.

### Check 4: No stray worktrees

```bash
git worktree list
git stash list
```

If unmerged ticket work exists — FAIL.

### Verdict

- ALL checks pass: verdict=PASS
- ANY check fails: verdict=FAIL with specific evidence

**Completion metadata:**
{verdict: "PASS"|"FAIL", branch_merged: true|false, no_dangling: true|false, tests_pass: true|false, all_tests: N, findings: ["..."]}
